name: checkbox
title: Checkbox
description: A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.
docs:
## When to use - One independent yes/no choice: accept the terms, remember this device, include archived items. - A set of choices where several can be true at once; use one checkbox per row. - A parent row that summarises children: pass `indeterminate` while the children disagree. - A table row selection, where each row is its own decision. ## When not to use - Exactly one of several options; use `radio-group`, which also gives arrow-key navigation. - An immediate setting that applies the moment it is flipped; use `switch`. - A formatting command that acts on a selection; use `toggle`. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox/checkbox"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label"; export function Terms() { return (
); } ``` `id` lands on the hidden input, so `htmlFor` on a `label` names the control and clicking the label toggles it. ## Examples ### Checked by default, and indeterminate ```tsx ``` `indeterminate` is a visual third state; `aria-checked="mixed"` is what a screen reader hears. It never replaces the checked state — pass `checked` too if the form needs a value. ### Controlled ```tsx const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(false); ; ``` ### Invalid, with a described error ```tsx

You must accept the terms to continue.

``` The ring turns destructive because `aria-invalid` is set. The component does not decide that anything is wrong. ### In a row of settings ```tsx

Every Monday, 09:00.

``` ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | `checked` | `boolean` | – | Controlled state. | | `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state. | | `onCheckedChange` | `(checked, details) => void` | – | Fired on click and on Space. | | `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Mixed visual state for a parent row. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignores interaction and form submission. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Focusable, submitted, not changeable. | | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission until checked. | | `name`, `value` | `string` | – | Form field identity and submitted value. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | All native attributes are forwarded, including `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. ## Motion contract Recipe: `state.morph`. The tick is the protagonist — it fades in and settles from 0.96 to full size when the box is checked, and reverses when it is cleared. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | | check | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes (re-click) | | clear | the same pair, reversed | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | `opacity` only | `state.morph` | yes | | none | no transition | – | – | Only the indicator moves. The box itself keeps a `transition-shadow` for the focus ring and the invalid ring, which is colour/shadow state feedback, not motion. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | `Tab` | Moves focus to the checkbox. | | `Space` | Toggles checked, unless `readOnly`. | | `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the previous control. | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders `role="checkbox"` on the visible element plus a hidden ``, so the control is in the form and in the tab order. - The tick is not the announcement: the state lives in `aria-checked`, which is why the reduced and `none` branches stay usable. - Always pair the box with a `Label` (`htmlFor`) or an `aria-label`; a bare box has no accessible name. - `indeterminate` announces as "mixed". Do not use it as a substitute for `checked` in a form. ## Validation and data ownership | The component does | You do | | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Styles `aria-invalid` and forwards it to the input | Deciding whether the box must be checked | | Forwards `required`, `name`, `value`, `disabled` | Building the submitted payload | | Announces `aria-checked` for all three states | Mapping the error to the field with `aria-describedby` | There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation). ## Responsive behavior The control is fixed at 16px with a 44px touch target (the `after:` pseudo element extends the hit area), so it behaves the same at every breakpoint. Put the label beside it, not inside it; wrapping a checkbox in a label removes the `aria-describedby` chain. ## Performance No JS animation loop: one Motion element per box, animating only `opacity` and `transform`. A list of 50 checkboxes is 50 short transitions on demand, never a running loop. ## Notes for AI - Use `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` for errors; there is no `error` prop. - Do not add press animation to a checkbox; the tick is the only protagonist. - For "one of N", use `radio-group`; for an instant setting, use `switch`.
